Welcome to Stockwell Primary School
We are delighted to welcome you to the Stockwell Primary School and Children’s Centre website (part of the BJS Federation of Schools), sharing the latest news, information, stories and successes from across our flourishing school.
We are a dynamic and vibrant primary school and pride ourselves on our wonderful pupils, our inspiring and creative teaching methods and our state-of-the-art learning environment.
Our passionate and dedicated team of staff are committed to ensuring your child is continuously encouraged, supported and challenged to develop their talents, uncover new interests and reach their full potential during their time with us, so that when they leave Stockwell they are prepared for their success at secondary school and beyond.
We continue to work in close partnership with our parents/carers to ensure you remain informed and involved in your child’s learning and development, and our regular communications between school and home, provide your child with the foundations for success.
We offer extensive and unique opportunities beyond the curriculum to enhance our pupils’ experience; our rich and varied extra-curriculum programme is one element of this and provides each child with the opportunity to learn new skills and develop their confidence.
Our Children’s Centre, located behind our school building, ensures our children have the best start in life. The centre provides a wide range of free activities and support services to families with children under the age of five.
We hope you enjoy exploring our website. However, please don’t hesitate to contact the school office on 020 7274 7687 for further information. We look forward to welcoming you to Stockwell Primary School and Children’s Centre.

Executive SENCo for the Federation
Hello Everyone, I am the Executive SENCo (Special Educational Needs Coordinator) for the Federation which means I get to work across all three schools. Ensuring that the profile of inclusion is raised and that there is a high level of consistency and continuity between the schools. My role is to coordinate the support for our learners who need additional support in some way to access the curriculum. I work alongside the head of Standards to ensure that the curriculum we are delivering is enabling all of our children.We are very proud of our schools and the fantastic work that we are doing to support all our learners, you will have a chance to hear what our current projects are when you read my newsletter.Now a little about me, I started my teaching career in Lambeth before moving to Wandsworth as a class teacher and science coordinator. Gaining my SENDCo qualification in 2014, I have worked across all primary phases and as Key stage one and lower key stage two phase leader ,while an Assistant head and my post prior to this one was Acting Deputy Headteacher for Inclusion.I live locally and I am a proud parent of two boys, who both attend Bonneville Primary School!

Uniform
Nursery
Children in the Nursery should wear comfortable, loose clothing which is easy to pull up and down, such as t-shirts, jogging pants and school sweatshirt. Please do not send your child in clothes which are difficult to manage. Dungarees and trousers with buttons/belt (or buttons on shirt sleeves) are very difficult for little ones to undo, especially when desperate for the toilet. Your child will be happier and more confident if they are able to dress/undress themselves. Please ensure your child wears comfortable shoes with fastenings they can manage themselves.
In the Nursery, your child will need a set of clothes in a named bag. Accidents do sometimes happen and, if it is not a case of getting to the toilet too late, it could be over-excitement in the water play!
If your child needs to borrow any items of clothing from the Nursery, please return them as soon as possible, washed and ready to wear.
Main School
We believe that the wearing of school uniform adds to the sense of community which should prevail in a school. The children look neat, attractive and not over or underdressed.

Times of the Day
Doors to the school building, supervised by members of the leadership team, will open at 8.50am where ‘Soft Start’ will commence. Soft Start encourages pupils to arrive to school before 9.00am, go straight to their class to carry out activities with their class teacher. Soft Start activities include Reading, Handwriting, English and Mathematics. These activities have a direct impact on all areas of the curriculum. The ‘Soft Start’ environment enables the children to settle down very quickly for the day, putting them in the right frame of mind for optimum learning. Soft Start also encourages independence and maturity when walking to your classroom and beginning your learning.

pageCache.text:
Science
Stockwell Primary School greatly understands the need for all pupils to develop their Scientific ability as an essential component of all subjects and as a subject in its own right. A good understanding of scientific knowledge and conceptual understanding helps to support pupils work across the curriculum, as well as enlighten their interactions with the world around them, act as a gateway to increase their own cultural capital and access all possibilities life has to offer.
Science Aims
At Stockwell Primary School Science is a body of knowledge built up through questioning, problem solving, investigations and the testing of ideas. Science is also a practical way of finding reliable answers to questions we may ask about the world around us. Science in our school is about developing children’s ideas and ways of working that enable them to make sense of the world in which they live. This is achieved through conducting different types of enquiry, using and applying Working Scientifically skills and communicating themselves clearly through the embedding and application of high level vocabulary.
Our teaching and learning
Science teaching at Stockwell Primary School involves an investigative led approach and includes careful questioning, the revisiting and drip feeding of key vocabulary in the context of different scientific concepts, and opportunities to learn and discover through exploration. Children will learn about six different scientists across every year of their primary school education to increase their cultural capital and expose them to the myriad of possibilities STEM subjects offer for later life. We acknowledge the paramount importance of adapting and extending our bespoke curriculum to match all pupils’ needs. Where possible, Science will be linked to class topics to ensure knowledge and understanding of the world is applied across a range of contexts and embedded in the long term memory through interleaving opportunities for application. Science will also be taught as discrete units and lessons where needed to ensure coverage. Throughout the year we have school trips and exciting visitors to stretch the learning experiences and broaden their understanding of possibilities through science within all year groups. We also identify gifted and talented pupils who are provided with extra challenges including trips to other schools within our cluster.

Year 6 have now begun rehearsals for their exciting end-of-year production of Aladdin. The children are throughly enjoying learning the songs and dances, and it’s been fantastic to see them stepping confidently into character following their successful auditions.
In Art & DT, pupils are busy designing and creating sets and props for the show. Their creativity, enthusiasm and teamwork are helping to bring the magical world of Aladdin to life, and we are very impressed with their imaginative ideas.
In Science, the children will be learning about different types of micro-organisms, including exploring the difference between helpful and harmful bacteria and the important roles they play in our everyday lives.
In Geography, pupils will be finding out what causes earthquakes, how they are measured and the impact they can have on communities around the world.
